tools.name: scale_recipe
tools.description:
Scale a recipe from 4 to 50 servings (serves), double or halve it, with head chef Cristopher's verified rules. Each line says why: straight maths, fixed ratio (garlic, onion, ginger, thickeners) or start low and taste up (salt in a soup), plus scaling-up tips: roasting, frying, stir-fry, braises, cakes, bread. Units: g, kg, ml, l, tsp, tbsp, lb, oz, cups. Refused, never guessed: allergen-free, curing, pickling, preserving and fermenting recipes. Only a 200 answer is charged; refusals are free.

Use for scaling ingredient quantities up or down (to double: fromPortions 1, toPortions 2). Not for nutrition, allergen or diet swaps, food safety, or scaling staff, labour, covers or money lines (a free 400). One amount per line: no ranges ("2-3 cloves"), no "1 lb 4 oz", no fl oz, pints or quarts; with cups, also give cupSize. A recipe with a line in cups may come back not chef-verified. Costs $0.01. Paid automatically in USDC with x402 (test USDC when this server is set to base-sepolia), within this server's per-session and per-day spend caps. Only a 200 answer is charged; 400, 404 and 422 are free. Set dryRun to true to check for free whether this would be answered and what it costs; nothing is signed. If unsure what is covered, call check_coverage first (free). Not every answer is chef-verified: say "chef-verified by Cristopher" only when the result's label says exactly that; otherwise say it is not chef-verified. A refusal is final: don't rephrase the question to get around it.

unit.description: Omit or null for counted items like eggs. mg is also accepted (converted to g), and cl, dl and hl (converted to ml). lb and oz are weight (never fluid ounces). cup or cups stay cups; "US cup(s)" or "metric cup(s)" also set the cup size. fl oz, pints, quarts, gallons, "c", "T" and "t" are rejected.

recipe.description: Text ("2 kg brisket; 500 ml stock; 1 tbsp salt; 3 eggs", ; or newline separated, one amount per line, max 200 characters a line) or structured lines. Max 40 lines. Mixed numbers ("1 1/2 kg") are read as one amount; "1,5 kg", "2-3 cloves" and "1 kg 500 g" are rejected.

method.description: Optional cooking method ("roast", "fry", "stir-fry") — selects method-specific tips. Screened like a question: a cure, ferment, preserve or holding method ("cold smoke", "pickling", "sous vide") is refused.

cupSize.description: Cup size for lines in cups: us = 236.5882365 ml, us-legal = 240 ml (US nutrition label), metric = 250 ml. Lines saying "US cups" or "metric cups" carry their own ("US cups" with us-legal is 240 ml); metric against a US size is rejected. Without a size, cups are scaled as cups with no ml and are not counted toward volume batch limits. Cups are never converted to grams, so they never count as a weight: a recipe with a line in cups gets no baker's percentage, and a rule that goes by the recipe's proportions by weight (salt in a cake or bread) can't be checked. When the recipe could be a cake or bread, its salt then scales straight as an engine default and the whole answer is labelled not chef-verified (the line's undecidedClass names the rule); when the known ingredients already rule that out (no flour, stock in it), the usual salt rule applies. Give weights to get the chef's rule.

tools.name: calculate_yield_and_cost
tools.description:
Raw vs cooked weight and cost per portion: what brisket yields after trim and cook loss, from head chef Cristopher's verified ranges. Send ingredient, weight bought, price paid, optional portions; get usable and cooked weight (best/mid/worst), cost per kg and per portion, with workings. Also whole salmon, pumpkin, onion, soft herbs (trim only); others 404 with suggestions. Refused, never guessed: allergen, curing and preserving terms. Only a 200 answer is charged; refusals and 404s are free.

Use when the user already bought, or has priced, a weight of one ingredient and wants what it yields and the cost per portion. For "how much do I need for N people", use calculate_amount_to_buy instead. ingredient must be an exact listed name or alias (others get a free 404 with suggestions). price is the total paid for purchased, not a price per kg. Give either portions (split the yield into N) or portionSize, not both. currency is required: the user's 3-letter currency code (display only). Costs $0.01. Paid automatically in USDC with x402 (test USDC when this server is set to base-sepolia), within this server's per-session and per-day spend caps. Only a 200 answer is charged; 400, 404 and 422 are free. Set dryRun to true to check for free whether this would be answered and what it costs; nothing is signed. If unsure what is covered, call check_coverage first (free). Not every answer is chef-verified: say "chef-verified by Cristopher" only when the result's label says exactly that; otherwise say it is not chef-verified. A refusal is final: don't rephrase the question to get around it.

purchased.description: Between 1 g and 10 t in total (0.0353 oz to 22,046 lb; lb and oz are converted exactly).

portions.description: Split the yield into this many portions: cooked when the chef has a cook-loss range for the ingredient, otherwise trimmed raw (`basis` says which). Not with portionSize.

portionSize.description: Weight of one portion as served: cooked when the chef has a cook-loss range for the ingredient, otherwise trimmed raw (`basis` says which). Not with portions.

tools.name: calculate_amount_to_buy
tools.description:
How much to buy: e.g. how much brisket for 120 people at 180 g cooked each. Send ingredient, portions and portion size (g, kg, lb, oz); get the weight to buy (best/mid/worst, rounded up) from head chef Cristopher's verified trim and cook-loss ranges. Add price per kg/lb and menu price ex GST/VAT for total cost, cost per portion and that ingredient's food cost %, with workings. Refused, never guessed: allergen, curing and preserving terms. Only a 200 answer is charged; refusals and 404s are free.

Use when the user starts from portions ("120 people, 180 g cooked each"). For "I bought 5 kg, what do I get", use calculate_yield_and_cost instead. portionSize is one portion as served (cooked when basis is cooked). For cost, give pricePerKg or pricePerLb (the price as bought; not both, and not "price"). sellPrice is the ex-tax menu price of one portion and needs one of them. currency is required: the user's 3-letter currency code (display only). Costs $0.01. Paid automatically in USDC with x402 (test USDC when this server is set to base-sepolia), within this server's per-session and per-day spend caps. Only a 200 answer is charged; 400, 404 and 422 are free. Set dryRun to true to check for free whether this would be answered and what it costs; nothing is signed. If unsure what is covered, call check_coverage first (free). Not every answer is chef-verified: say "chef-verified by Cristopher" only when the result's label says exactly that; otherwise say it is not chef-verified. A refusal is final: don't rephrase the question to get around it.

portionSize.description: Weight of one portion as served — cooked when the chef has a cook-loss range for the ingredient, otherwise trimmed raw (the response's `basis` says which). portions × portionSize is at most 10 t.

tools.name: diagnose_cooking_problem
tools.description:
Why is my bread dense? Hollandaise split? Rice gluggy? Send a dish and a symptom; get the likely cause and head chef Cristopher's verified fix. Answered: bread or pizza dough dense, hollandaise or bearnaise split, rice mushy, mash gluey, roast veg soggy, seared meat grey, caramel grainy, pastry shrinking, muffins tough, chicken breast dry, garlic bitter. Refused, never guessed: allergens, storage, leftovers, reheating, safe temperatures. Only a 200 answer is charged; refusals and 404s are free.

Send the dish and a short symptom in the user's words ("dense", "split", "came out gluey"). Leave out extra clauses ("…after I added the butter"). Rescue questions ("can I save it?") aren't answered, and "is it still safe?" is refused. An unlisted dish or symptom gets a free 404 with the valid names. Retry only if the user's dish really is one of them; don't swap in a different dish. Costs $0.02. Only a 200 answer is charged; 400, 404 and 422 are free. Set dryRun to true to check for free whether this would be answered and what it costs; nothing is signed. Not every answer is chef-verified: say "chef-verified by Cristopher" only when the result's label says exactly that; otherwise say it is not chef-verified. tools.name: find_ingredient_substitute
tools.description:
What can I use instead of buttermilk, self-raising flour, creme fraiche or sour cream? Get head chef Cristopher's verified swaps: yes, no or depends (and on what), with amount and context where given, including swaps not to make. Also fresh herbs, butter, oil, sugar, flour, fresh tomatoes, fresh stock, whole spices; others get a 404 listing them. Refused, never guessed: allergens and dairy-, egg- or gluten-free swaps, storage, preserving. Only a 200 answer is charged; refusals and 404s are free.

ingredient is what the user wants to replace. use is optional: the replacement they have in mind, to get just that answer. A "no" verdict is advice too: pass it on, with what it depends on for "depends". Allergy, dairy-, egg- or gluten-free and storage framings are refused (free 422). Costs $0.01. Paid automatically in USDC with x402 (test USDC when this server is set to base-sepolia), within this server's per-session and per-day spend caps.
